alt: A grid of pass and fail marks. Rows: the correct engine, an engine that charges sellers the maker fee instead of the taker fee, and an engine that never delivers trade messages. Under the original checker all three pass and are paid for speed; under the fixed checker, which also runs 33 of the project's own tests, the correct engine passes and both broken engines are rejected with a score of 0. Notes explain the speed score (0 at 2.09 million transactions per second or slower, 100 at 6 million), give the overlapping speed scores (correct engine 0–24.19, wrong fee 7.77–24.40, lost messages 4.71–15.62 out of 100), and say that at 4 CPUs even the correct engine scores 0 for speed.
caption: Two engines with realistic bugs pass the original checker and are paid for speed; the fixed checker rejects them. The agent must make a stock-exchange matching engine faster without changing what it does, but the original checker only confirms that money balances overall and that the order books match, so an engine that charges selling traders the wrong fee and one that never delivers trade messages both pass and get a speed score out of 100 (7.77–24.40 and 4.71–15.62 over four runs each, against 0–24.19 for the correct engine over seven; the differences are run-to-run variation). The fixed checker first runs 33 of the project's own tests: both broken engines score 0 in all three side-by-side runs, and the correct engine still passes, also in three runs at the leaderboard's 4 CPUs, where it is too slow to score above 0 for speed.
